skill.name: vercel-cli-with-tokens
skill.description: Deploy and manage Vercel projects with token-based CLI authentication instead of interactive login.
skill.summary: Guides token-based Vercel CLI setup, deployments, project linking, and environment management.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives because SKILL.md is documentation, not executable Ruby or JavaScript. Confirmed issues are the intended handling of Vercel tokens and env files, plus automation that can mutate Vercel deployments, environment variables, domains, and confirmations. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid printing full tokens, prefer narrow variable lookups over broad env scans, and mask any secret values in assistant output.

remediation.issue: Pulling Vercel environment variables to local files
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before pulling env values, warn that secrets may be written to disk, and suggest cleanup after use.
Use -y only after explicit user approval for the exact production, domain, env, or deployment action being performed.
Ask before installing global packages and prefer an existing local CLI or temporary runner when possible.

content.value_statement: Interactive Vercel login can block AI-assisted deployment workflows. This skill guides token-based CLI setup, preview deployments, project linking, and environment management.
actual_capabilities: Finds Vercel token, project, and organization values in environment variables or local env files.
Sets up Vercel CLI usage with token-based authentication and team scope selection.
Deploys preview builds by default and documents production deploys only when requested.
Links local or remote repositories to Vercel projects using CLI workflows.
Manages Vercel environment variables, domains, deployment inspection, and build logs.
limitations: Requires a valid Vercel token with permissions for the target team and project.
Can read local env files and handle secrets, so outputs must be reviewed for token exposure.
Cannot guarantee a deployment will succeed when project dependencies or Vercel settings are invalid.
Production deploys, git pushes, domain changes, and env changes still need explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Deploy a preview build
use_cases.description: Prepare token authentication and run a preview deployment without interactive Vercel login.

use_cases.title: Connect a repository to Vercel
use_cases.description: Link a local or cloned repository to the correct Vercel project and team scope.

use_cases.title: Operate Vercel from an AI assistant
use_cases.description: Guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through safe CLI-based Vercel workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Vercel CLI token workflow to deploy this project as a preview. Confirm the token source and return the deployment link.

prompt_templates.title: Link the project
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the correct Vercel team and project identifiers, then link this repository to the matching Vercel project.

prompt_templates.title: Update environment variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Add or update the required Vercel environment variables for preview and production. Ask before changing production values.

prompt_templates.title: Run a controlled release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review project state, confirm git and Vercel scope, request approval for production deployment, then deploy and inspect the result.

output_examples.input: Deploy this app to Vercel as a preview using my token.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the token source, confirms the project scope, starts a preview deployment, and returns the Vercel deployment URL.

output_examples.input: Set the API endpoint for my Vercel project.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the value, confirms the target environment, applies the variable through Vercel CLI, and summarizes the changed setting.

output_examples.input: Check why the latest Vercel build failed.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists recent deployments, opens the relevant build logs, and reports the likely cause with the next corrective step.

best_practices: Use preview deployments by default and require explicit approval for production changes.
Keep Vercel tokens out of command arguments, shell history, logs, and shared transcripts.
Confirm team scope, project ID, and environment target before changing Vercel resources.
anti_patterns: Passing a Vercel token through a command-line flag or pasting it into public output.
Using confirmation bypass flags for production, domain, or environment changes without user approval.
Deploying from an unverified repository or team scope.

faq.question: Does this skill require interactive Vercel login?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for workflows that use Vercel access tokens instead of browser-based login.

faq.question: Can it deploy to production?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill says production deployment should happen only when the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: Does it manage environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows to add, list, pull, and remove Vercel environment variables.

faq.question: Is token handling a security risk?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow may inspect environment variables and env files, so secrets must be masked and handled carefully.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it verify deployed URLs by fetching them?
faq.answer: No. The skill says to return the deployment link without fetching the deployed URL.
